html:
A battle fought over several days in August 636 near the Yarmuk River, east of the Sea of Galilee, in which the Arab Muslim army of the Rashidun Caliphate destroyed a large Byzantine army. It decided the fate of Syria.

After Arab forces took Damascus in 634 to 635, Emperor Heraclius gathered a big army of Romans, Armenians and Arab allies to win Syria back. The Muslims pulled back to open ground by the Yarmuk. Commanded in the field by Khalid ibn al-Walid, their mobile cavalry pinned the Byzantines against the river gorges and cut off their retreat. Divisions among the Byzantine commanders made things worse.

The defeat ended Roman rule in Syria and Palestine. Heraclius left the province, and Jerusalem surrendered to the caliph Umar about two years later. With Egypt lost soon after, the Eastern Roman Empire shrank to Anatolia and the Balkans and had to reorganise to survive, which led to the theme system. It was a key moment in the Arab conquests.
